issues.description: Method Milkable.messageOnMilk(): The problem statement (UML and textual requirements) declares Milkable.messageOnMilk() as returning boolean (UML shows messageOnMilk():boolean and Part 2 text says “should return true/false”), but the provided solution repository defines the interface method as returning String (solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java: String messageOnMilk()) and the concrete classes Seal and Goat implement messageOnMilk() to return descriptive Strings (e.g., "Goat <name> is milked"). The template Main prints m.messageOnMilk(), which works for either type when printed but does not resolve the signature conflict. This mismatch leaves students unsure which return type to implement and will cause compilation/test failures if different artifacts are followed.
issues.suggestedFix:
Unify the return type across all artifacts. Two consistent options (choose one):

Option A (recommended to match current solution): Change the problem statement and UML to require Milkable.messageOnMilk() to return String and update the descriptive text to explain that the method returns a user-facing message (e.g., "Goat <name> is milked"). Update any tests and template comments to expect a String. Ensure UML shows messageOnMilk():String and Part 2 text is updated accordingly.

Option B: Change the solution to match the problem statement by making Milkable.messageOnMilk() return boolean. Update solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Milkable.java to declare boolean messageOnMilk(), modify Goat and Seal to return true/false and adjust their implementations and any tests or Main usage to handle boolean return values (e.g., print success/failure messages elsewhere).

Apply the chosen change to: problem statement (UML and Part 2 text), template code comments/Main usage, the interface declaration, and all concrete implementations/tests so that every artifact uses the same signature and behavior.
